text:
Recent work supports incorporating item text, but this search found no verified 2024–2026 study matching every constraint: BERT4Rec backbone, lightweight title/description encoder trained entirely from scratch, and one jointly trained predictor. [MARS (CIKM 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) motivates finer distinctions through attribute-aware text representations and attribute-wise user–item matching, within the pretrained-language-model paradigm. [Q-BERT4Rec (December 2025; revised March 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02474) directly extends BERT4Rec with semantic feature injection, residual vector quantization, and multiple masking strategies. Its multimodal, multistage design does not establish the effectiveness of a small, from-scratch text encoder.

A constraint-compatible experiment, inferred from these ideas: tokenize only supplied titles/descriptions; learn small word or hashed-subword embeddings with mean pooling and a projection; combine text and item-ID embeddings through a jointly learned residual gate. Share the resulting item representation between history encoding and candidate scoring, training everything with masked-item cross-entropy in one BERT4Rec checkpoint per category. Retain a dedicated mask embedding and remove the masked item’s text alongside its ID to prevent target leakage; append a mask for inference, following [BERT4Rec’s formulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690). Compare against the corrected ID-only baseline using macro validation HR@10. Shared lexical parameters could help sparse items, but benefits remain a hypothesis: weak interaction supervision, generic descriptions, and over-smoothing between similar products may limit gains.
